subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should Slack support an explicit user-identity DM mode that accepts user-authorized message.im events and replies with xoxp tokens, or should OpenClaw keep bot/app identity as the only supported inbound DM path?
rationale: The requested behavior would let OpenClaw act as a regular Slack user, while current docs and tests treat userToken as read-oriented and keep bot-token writes preferred when a bot token exists.

options.title: Add explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Design a named opt-in mode with authorization-scoped inbound routing, matching xoxp reply-token selection, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Keep bot-only DMs
options.body: Document that user-level Slack event subscriptions are unsupported and keep DMs routed through the Slack app/bot identity.

options.title: Verify read-only first
options.body: Add diagnostics for user-token scopes and delivered authorizations while deferring send-as-user behavior until the security model is approved.

recommendation.title: Add explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Design a named opt-in mode with authorization-scoped inbound routing, matching xoxp reply-token selection, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently worked on Slack per-event scope handling, which is the closest current-main decision surface for this authorization model.
